views.name: superhero_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  superhero.id AS id,
  superhero.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  superhero.full_name AS full_name,
  superhero.gender_id AS gender_id,
  superhero.eye_colour_id AS eye_colour_id,
  superhero.hair_colour_id AS hair_colour_id,
  superhero.skin_colour_id AS skin_colour_id,
  superhero.race_id AS race_id,
  superhero.publisher_id AS publisher_id,
  superhero.alignment_id AS alignment_id,
  superhero.height_cm AS height_cm,
  superhero.weight_kg AS weight_kg
FROM superhero
views.description: One row per superhero with canonical identifying and demographic columns resolved to ids and raw values for downstream filters and joins.
validated_on: How many gold-eyed superheroes did Marvel Comics publish?
What is Copycat's race?
How many female superheroes have a strength value of 100?
What is the total number of superheroes without full name?
What is the average weight of all female superheroes?
List down at least five superpowers of male superheroes.
Among the superheroes with height from 170 to 190, list the names of the superheroes with no eye color.
In superheroes with height between 150 to 180, what is the percentage of heroes published by Marvel Comics?
Among the male superheroes, list the super hero names of superheroes with weight greater than the 79% average weight of all superheroes.
Which superhero has the same eyes, hair and skin colour? Indicate the publisher of the superhero.

views.name: superhero_powers
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  hero_power.hero_id AS hero_id,
  hero_power.power_id AS power_id,
  superpower.power_name AS power_name
FROM hero_power
JOIN superpower ON superpower.id = hero_power.power_id
views.description: Mapping of each superhero to each superpower they possess (denormalized join of hero_power to superpower). One row per hero-power association.
validated_on: Among the superheroes with the super power of "Super Strength", how many of them have a height of over 200cm?

views.description: Attributes and their numeric values for each superhero (denormalized join of hero_attribute to attribute). One row per hero-attribute pair.

views.name: superhero_core_7
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.id,
  s.superhero_name,
  s.full_name,
  s.gender_id,
  g.gender AS gender,
  s.eye_colour_id,
  ec.colour AS eye_colour,
  s.hair_colour_id,
  hc.colour AS hair_colour,
  s.skin_colour_id,
  sc.colour AS skin_colour,
  s.race_id,
  r.race AS race,
  s.publisher_id,
  p.publisher_name,
  s.alignment_id,
  a.alignment AS alignment,
  s.height_cm,
  s.weight_kg
FROM superhero s
LEFT JOIN gender g ON s.gender_id = g.id
LEFT JOIN colour ec ON s.eye_colour_id = ec.id
LEFT JOIN colour hc ON s.hair_colour_id = hc.id
LEFT JOIN colour sc ON s.skin_colour_id = sc.id
LEFT JOIN race r ON s.race_id = r.id
LEFT JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN alignment a ON s.alignment_id = a.id
views.description: One row per superhero with denormalized foreign-key ids and textual labels for related dimensions (gender, race, publisher, alignment, eye/hair/skin colours). Keeps raw numeric measures (height_cm, weight_kg) and keys for attributes/powers to be joined separately.

views.name: publisher_distinct_for_heroes
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.id AS publisher_id,
  p.publisher_name AS publisher_name,
  COUNT(s.id) AS hero_count
FROM publisher p
LEFT JOIN superhero s
  ON s.publisher_id = p.id
GROUP BY p.id, p.publisher_name
views.description: One row per publisher exposing publisher id and publisher_name and the count of heroes associated. Useful to return distinct publishers for a cohort of heroes (the cohort filter is applied in question_ops).

views.name: superhero_with_publisher_and_basic_attrs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  sc.id,
  sc.superhero_name,
  sc.full_name,
  sc.publisher_id,
  p.publisher_name,
  sc.gender_id,
  g.gender,
  sc.alignment_id,
  a.alignment,
  sc.race_id,
  r.race,
  sc.height_cm,
  sc.weight_kg,
  sc.eye_colour_id,
  sc.hair_colour_id,
  sc.skin_colour_id
FROM superhero_core sc
LEFT JOIN publisher p ON sc.publisher_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN gender g ON sc.gender_id = g.id
LEFT JOIN alignment a ON sc.alignment_id = a.id
LEFT JOIN race r ON sc.race_id = r.id
WHERE sc.publisher_id IS NOT NULL
  AND p.publisher_name IS NOT NULL
views.description: One row per superhero enriched with its publisher name and basic identifying attributes (keeps raw numeric measures). Useful as a base cohort for counting or filtering superheroes by publisher, gender, alignment, race, and colors.

views.name: publisher_superhero_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.id AS id,
  s.publisher_id AS publisher_id,
  p.publisher_name AS publisher_name
FROM superhero s
JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id
WHERE s.publisher_id IS NOT NULL
  AND p.publisher_name IS NOT NULL
views.description: Cohort of superheroes with non-null publisher and publisher_name exposed. One row per superhero intended for counts/filters by publisher. No aggregation performed here so it's reusable for many question-level aggregates.

views.name: superhero_attribute_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ha.hero_id AS hero_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT ha.attribute_id) AS num_attributes,
  MIN(ha.attribute_value) AS min_attribute_value,
  MAX(ha.attribute_value) AS max_attribute_value,
  AVG(ha.attribute_value) AS avg_attribute_value
FROM hero_attribute ha
GROUP BY ha.hero_id
views.description: Per-superhero summary of attribute counts and presence. Aggregates hero_attribute to one row per superhero with counts of distinct attributes and raw attribute_value stats. Useful for future questions needing per-hero attribute-level measures while preserving grain at superhero.id.

views.name: superhero_core_denorm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.id AS id,
  s.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  s.full_name AS full_name,
  s.publisher_id AS publisher_id,
  p.publisher_name AS publisher_name,
  s.gender_id AS gender_id,
  g.gender AS gender,
  s.alignment_id AS alignment_id,
  a.alignment AS alignment,
  s.race_id AS race_id,
  r.race AS race,
  s.eye_colour_id AS eye_colour_id,
  ec.colour AS eye_colour,
  s.hair_colour_id AS hair_colour_id,
  hc.colour AS hair_colour,
  s.skin_colour_id AS skin_colour_id,
  sc.colour AS skin_colour,
  s.height_cm AS height_cm,
  s.weight_kg AS weight_kg
FROM superhero s
LEFT JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN gender g ON s.gender_id = g.id
LEFT JOIN alignment a ON s.alignment_id = a.id
LEFT JOIN race r ON s.race_id = r.id
LEFT JOIN colour ec ON s.eye_colour_id = ec.id
LEFT JOIN colour hc ON s.hair_colour_id = hc.id
LEFT JOIN colour sc ON s.skin_colour_id = sc.id
views.description: Denormalized row per superhero combining key identity, publisher, and classification attributes (gender, alignment, race, and colours) to make filtering by those dimensions easy.

views.name: hero_attribute_measures
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  hero_attribute.hero_id AS hero_id,
  hero_attribute.attribute_id AS attribute_id,
  attribute.attribute_name AS attribute_name,
  hero_attribute.attribute_value AS attribute_value
FROM hero_attribute
JOIN attribute ON attribute.id = hero_attribute.attribute_id
views.description: Row-level measures for each hero-attribute combination exposing raw attribute values and attribute names, suitable for filtering to a specific attribute (e.g., durability) and aggregating or ranking at the hero level.

views.name: hero_top_attribute_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  hav.hero_id AS hero_id,
  hav.attribute_id AS attribute_id,
  a.attribute_name AS attribute_name,
  hav.attribute_value AS attribute_value,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (
    PARTITION BY hav.attribute_id
    ORDER BY hav.attribute_value DESC
  ) AS attr_rank_desc
FROM hero_attribute AS hav
JOIN attribute AS a
  ON a.id = hav.attribute_id
views.description: Per-attribute ranking of heroes by attribute_value. Produces a row per hero-attribute with a dense_rank (or row_number) so callers can pick top-N heroes for any attribute.

views.name: colour_lookup_30
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  colour.id AS id,
  colour.colour AS colour
FROM colour
WHERE colour.id IN (
  SELECT DISTINCT eye_colour_id FROM superhero WHERE eye_colour_id IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT hair_colour_id FROM superhero WHERE hair_colour_id IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT skin_colour_id FROM superhero WHERE skin_colour_id IS NOT NULL
)
views.description: Canonical colour id to colour text mapping for colours referenced by superheroes.

views.name: superhero_with_demographics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.id AS id,
  s.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  s.full_name AS full_name,
  s.gender_id AS gender_id,
  g.gender AS gender,
  s.publisher_id AS publisher_id,
  p.publisher_name AS publisher_name,
  s.eye_colour_id AS eye_colour_id,
  s.hair_colour_id AS hair_colour_id,
  s.skin_colour_id AS skin_colour_id
FROM superhero s
LEFT JOIN gender g ON s.gender_id = g.id
LEFT JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id
views.description: Denormalized superhero rows joined to gender and publisher (text) to form a cohort usable for filtering by gender or publisher name. Keeps colour id columns for later resolution to colour text via colour_lookup.

views.name: superheroes_same_eye_hair_skin
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  superhero_name,
  publisher_id,
  eye_colour_id,
  hair_colour_id,
  skin_colour_id
FROM
  superhero
WHERE
  eye_colour_id = hair_colour_id
  AND hair_colour_id = skin_colour_id
views.description: Cohort of superheroes whose eye_colour_id, hair_colour_id and skin_colour_id are all equal (one row per superhero). Keeps core id and name and publisher_id for joining to publisher details later.
